 'It's unbelievable for the town' published at 23:02 GMT 23:02 GMT 
 FT: Fleetwood 1-1 Arsenal (5-3 pens) 
 BBC Radio 5 Live 
 More from Fleetwood's Jake Batty to BBC Radio 5 Live : "We have struggled. We're not known as a big club in League Two, and we get a few thousand fans each game.
 "The buzz around town, the fans didn't shut up all game, and that's what we encourage [everyone] to bring on Saturday.
 "Just because it's Bristol Rovers on Saturday and not Arsenal at home, why can't we replicate that and get 5,000 fans behind us every game and give us that momentum. Every single one of us is so happy and proud of all the fans that turned out today.
 "That's exactly what we need. Because without them, we would have struggled in the moments when they were giving us an extra lift. You think bloody hell, there are a lot of people here supporting me, wanting me to do well. It's unbelievable for the town. I don't think we should be scared of anyone, or any team now."

 'I cannot fault at all the attitude of the players' published at 22:59 GMT 22:59 GMT 
 FT: Fleetwood 1-1 Arsenal (5-3 pens) 
 Arsenal 
 Image source, Getty Images Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta, speaking to Sky Sports: "First of all, congratulations to Fleetwood for going through in the next round, in the manner they've done it, the atmosphere they have created, and, yeah, a really sad day for us.
 "I cannot fault at all the attitude of the players. I haven't seen anyone not doing what is required at this level. But, obviously, we insisted so much, we have so much of the ball, so many chances, so many shots, and if you want the margins to be bigger than going to the penalties, obviously, you need to capitalize on that. And we didn't. And football is about that.
 "It is, and especially when they go ahead and, and they create that momentum. We gave them almost nothing in the whole game and we created so many chances, and didn't capitalise on that. And then the margins become so small, that's it. This football, that's the beauty as well of this competition, and, especially in this country, it's a very sad day."
 On Max Dowman's red card: "It's difficult to see on the cameras like that, so I prefer to watch it back properly and then I can assess the situation."
 On if Dowman will learn from this: "Yeah, we'll learn from everything."
 On if he saw enough: "Yeah, the attitude-wise, I have zero. Otherwise, I would be here absolutely fuming. I'm sad, I think we are all sad. We have a massive responsibility to carry this badge in the best possible way. It had nothing to do with effort or application or determination to win it, but we lack other things to, to create a much bigger margin than today, with what we produce, they really should have been shown in the scoreline."
 76 85 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'I don't think we should be scared of anyone, or any team now' published at 22:57 GMT 22:57 GMT 
 FT: Fleetwood 1-1 Arsenal (5-3 pens) 
 Fleetwood defender Jake Batty, speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live: "The champions of England coming to our patch, we always knew it was going to be a tough game, we always knew we were going to have to grind out a result. 
 "I think 1-1 was probably a fair result over 90 minutes, I think we did what we needed to do, I think everyone stuck to the game plan, but yeah, it gives us so much confidence, so much motivation, and it brings us lads closer together because we know we can trust each other arguably against the best players in the world at the moment."
 On if the occasion was extra motivation: "We have to replicate that every game. Our league form hasn't been as good as what we wanted it to be, and for some reason, cup competitions give everyone a bit more fire in the belly. We just came up with some magical moments, and this one, is one to tell the grandkids."
 On hanging on: "We knew they were going to come here and dominate the ball. We're not silly, we know what we are, we know what they are. Obviously, when they got the goal early in the second half, you're thinking 'oh god, here we go', but I think the resistance, the communication, and the culture of the lads. 
 "Everyone is just doing a job for each other, fighting for their own place, which is what they need, and we need to go onto Saturday, and carry that momentum and confidence into the game to get three points. We knew we would give [Arsenal] a good game on our patch, and we knew the crowd was going to be there for us."
 On Arsenal: "I think we kept them quite in places that we needed to keep them quite and I just think, you can't stop that type of experience."

 Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta, speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live: "First of all, congratulations to Fleetwood for going through the next round. The manner that they have done it, and for us a very sad day. 
 "There is nothing to criticise the players for their attitude, their application. The determination - you could see that was there from the start. Even with 10 men, we conceded a really poor goal to start with that gave them some momentum."
 141 79 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'The biggest night in the club's history' published at 22:49 GMT 22:49 GMT 
 FT: Fleetwood 1-1 Arsenal (5-3 pens) 
 Fleetwood Town boss Matt Lawlor, speaking to Sky Sports: "It's really hard to address the players. I've just said to enjoy it and then we've got a league game on Saturday and I didn't want to be the bearer of the reality, but we've got a game. I just can't believe it. The biggest night in the club's history in terms of opposition coming to town and we've managed to beat the champions.
 "We knew before the game, we're not stupid enough and not egotistical enough that you think we're going to go to the best team in the country and the most organised team in the country and the best of the basics and the world-class players, in that we're going to go and outplay them. So we had to ride our luck, we had to deny space, we had to deny options for them. And I think we did that really, really well in terms of the majority of the game. Obviously, the goal happens, but they're going to happen; they're so good at football. The footballers that they have, the gaps that they find and we see it every week in the Premier League.
 "I'm a big football fan and I watch the National League all the way through to the Premier League, Championship. So for me it was a tough game to prepare for, but I'm just so glad that the lads have the feeling the way they are and took that performance into make that town, the club, everyone proud."

 By Emily Salley BBC Sport journalist Fleetwood Town pulled off one of the biggest upsets in Carabao Cup history as they beat Premier League champions Arsenal in an astounding penalty shootout to reach the quarter-finals. 
 Mikel Arteta's side were left shell-shocked when Aaron Loupalo-Bi gave the hosts - ranked 84 places below the Gunners in the football pyramid - an unexpected lead in the 21st minute.
 Viktor Gyokeres pulled the visitors level after the break, but a wasteful Arsenal side could not put the game to bed and they were reduced to 10-men in the 86th minute when teenage starlet Max Dowman kicked out after a hefty tackle by Harrison Neal.
 Jay Lynch made two sublime saves to stop Ben White and Martin Odegaard right at the death to take the hosts to penalty shootout.
 And the Fleetwood goalkeeper pulled off more heroics as he stopped Bruno Guimaraes' spot kick before Conor Haughey sparked scenes of ecstasy at Highbury Stadium by converting the winning penalty.
 Fans flooded onto the pitch, players swore in their post-match interviews, while manager Matt Lawlor was reduced to tears during the emphatic celebrations.
 Fleetwood will find out their quarter-final opponents when the draw takes place following the conclusion of Chelsea's game against Liverpool on Wednesday.
 Arsenal analysis: Wasteful Premier League champions left dumbstruck 
 Arsenal were welcomed by flames and fireworks, but the game had barely got going before referee Michael Salisbury stopped play after spotting a drone flying above Highbury Stadium.
 The match re-started eight minutes later - after the players had briefly been instructed to leave the pitch - and Arsenal were soon caught off guard when Loupalo-Bi rolled Marli Salmon and slotted past Illan Meslier.
 Despite having countless chances and dominating possession, Arteta's side trailed at the break - much to the delight of the raucous home crowd.
 But the Fleetwood's elation did not last long as Gyokeres scrambled in the six-yard box to poke home an equaliser four minutes into the second half.
 Introduced at half-time, captain Martin Odegaard had injected a sense of urgency into the team, but they still lacked a clinical edge - with only one goal to show for 26 shots and 59 touches inside the Fleetwood box.
 Their evening in the north west went from bad to worse when 16-year-old Dowman saw red, kicking out at Neal before facing the wrath of Arteta as he headed down the tunnel.
 Meslier, making his debut for the Gunners, failed to get close to any of the Cod Army's penalty kicks, while it was a lacklustre strike from Guimaraes that sealed the Gunners' fate.
 Fleetwood analysis: League Two minnows defy the odds 
 With Fleetwood languishing in 18th in the English fourth division, Arteta made nine changes from Saturday's win over Everton - opting for a blend of youthful talent and Premier League non-starters.
 Making just his second senior appearance for Arsenal, Salmon lacked the physicality needed to hold off Loupalo-Bi before the Fulham loanee jabbed the ball through Meslier's legs - and the 17-year-old defender was hauled off at half-time.
 Fleetwood's defenders, meanwhile, gave everything to keep Arsenal at bay, with Rhys Bennett, Conor Haughey and Shaun Rooney all throwing themselves in front of every shot as they weathered wave upon wave of relentless pressure.
 The home fans - perhaps expecting Arsenal to open the floodgates at some stage - took delight in their side's ability to hold on for so long , and chants of "champions of England, you're having a laugh" echoed around Highbury Stadium.
 Ultimately, it came down to conviction. Ronan Coughlan, Neal, Will Davies, Andy Cannon and Haughey each slammed their penalties emphatically past Meslier, showing a fearlessness that stood in stark contrast to Arsenal's timid overall performance.
